newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude softer, markets awaits Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude softer, markets awaits Iraq news.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil oscillated sharply before lunch and then lost ground as a disappointing NYMEX gasoline opening pressured prices in a market awaiting further news on Iraq, brokers said.
"There was a bit of a peak at lunchtime but the (NYMEX) gasoline opening was disappointing and the U.S. is now looking to test the bottom end of the range," one said.
September Brent crude oil traded down two cents at $18.93 a barrel by 1447 GMT after the contract earlier moved at an intraday high of $19.08 a barrel.

September WTI crude lost 16 cents to $20.12 a barrel. Brokers saw resistance on September Brent at $19.00 as difficult to break while the market waited for the U.N. decision on the Iraqi aid distribution plan.

"The market expects the agreement to be this afternoon so it's a bit of a standoff. But I'm not so confident there will be a big sell-off. People who said a week ago that we would see 50 cents off the market on the news are now talking about a 20 cent drop," the broker added.
August gas oil traded last up one dollar at $172.50 a tonne in a thinly traded market.
Many traders and analysts were of the opinion that lean global stocks should prevent crude prices going into an immediate tailspin once Iraqi crude oil exports restart.
U.N spokesman Fred Eckhard said last Thursday that Iraq's aid distribution plan was expected to gain U.N. approval early this week.
